findings.claim: The agent's token refusal still says "Give it only to the step that posts the report", and the how-to quotes it. Since this change no step in the agent's job gets the token; only the separate publish job does, so the message now sends the reader toward the setup the ticket removed.

verdict.text: The change can land after one small wording fix.

`publish` does what the plan says: it creates the issue, or edits it and adds a comment with the mentions; below the threshold it closes an open issue with a comment; owners come from the last `*` rule of the first CODEOWNERS file; it exits 1 when gh fails and 2 for a bad report.
The token and the agent are kept apart as the three plan rounds required: the audit job has `contents: read`, no token and no cache.
The publish job is a fresh runner with `issues: write`, a checkout with `persist-credentials: false`, setup-uv with the cache off, and the artifact downloaded into `$RUNNER_TEMP`.
One finding, not blocking: the agent's refusal message, and the how-to's quote of it, still tell users to give the token to "the step that posts the report".
`loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: lint, format, tests and integration pass, rows r1 to r7 pass, "stamp green: 25f04f65ae90ac4c8e03fdaa021222322fa03168eab2dcd8c125f6563446148a".
Read the whole diff in action/agent.py, action.yml, the workflow, both test files, scripts/release.py and its tests, ADRs 0012 and 0017, the overview, the log and the how-to.
r1: `test_publish_below_threshold_posts_nothing` asserts no create, edit, comment or close.
`..._closes_open_issue` asserts a comment on #7 that names the threshold, then a close, in that order, and no create or edit.
r2: create with the default title, both findings in the body and the run link.
Edit on #7 rather than a create, plus a comment with `@alice` and "2 high".
The stub lists "Knowledge audit 2", which also checks exact title matching.
r3: last `*` rule wins and comments are stripped.
.github/ beats the root file, which beats docs/.
`--mention` replaces the owners and gets an `@` added when missing.
With no owners there is no cc line.
r4: a failing gh exits 1 and creates nothing.
A missing file, bad JSON or a report without findings exits 2 with a message and no gh call.
r5: tests check workflow-level permissions are exactly `contents: read`, that the audit job sets none and holds no token.
The publish job has `needs: audit` and `{contents: read, issues: write}`.
Every setup-uv sets `enable-cache: false` and no actions/cache is used.
In the action, only the publish step holds the token, and the new inputs are wired through env (no `${{ }}` in the shell text).
r6: `kmctl check` is clean and nothing names knowledge-audit-issue.sh.

r8 (judgment): `uv run --script action/agent.py publish --help` lists report, --min-severity (choices and Default: high), --title (Default: Knowledge audit), --mention (Repeatable, default the CODEOWNERS owners) and --repo (Default: the current folder), with exit codes in the description.
That meets the row.
release.py: the new `- uses: JasperHG90/Knowledge-management@v0.3.0` line in the how-to matches `_USES`, so DOC_LINES 6 is right.
ADR 0012 has a correction recording it.

f1 (open, docs, non-blocking): action/agent.py:481 and docs/how-to/install-the-plugin-and-the-ci-action.md:342 should say to give the token only to the publish job (a separate job), not to "the step that posts the report".
Update both together.
A report larger than GitHub's 65536-character body limit makes gh fail, and publish exits 1.
The old shell script behaved the same way, so this is no regression.
In action.yml's publish mode, CODEOWNERS is read from `inputs.path`.
With a subfolder `path`, a root CODEOWNERS is not found.
The default "." is fine.
